questions.q: What is Action Designer used for?
options: Building a custom, reusable action so multiple flows can call the same logic instead of duplicating it
Designing the visual layout of a flow's canvas
Creating new Notification templates
Approving records inside the Approvals module
questions.explain: Action Designer lets you build custom actions once, so every flow that needs that logic calls the same action rather than re-implementing it.

questions.q: What are the three parts of any custom action built in Action Designer?
options: Inputs, internal steps, and Outputs
Triggers, conditions, and loops
A table, a view, and a form
A subflow, a flow, and a stage
questions.explain: Every custom action defines what data it needs (Inputs), what it does with it (internal steps), and what it hands back (Outputs).

questions.q: In the 'Calculate SLA Due Date' example, what does the action's Output provide to the calling flow?
options: The calculated due date, usable as a data pill in later steps
A new Incident record created from scratch
A completed approval decision
A fired Notification confirming SLA compliance
questions.explain: The custom action's Output is the calculated due date, which the calling flow consumes as a data pill just like any built-in action's output.

questions.q: What can the internal steps of a custom action include?
options: Built-in actions, scripting steps, or even IntegrationHub actions
Only built-in actions, never scripting
Only IntegrationHub actions
Nothing — a custom action cannot contain any steps of its own
questions.explain: Internal steps can mix built-in actions, scripting for custom logic, and IntegrationHub actions if the action needs to reach outside the platform.

questions.q: What's the real cost of copy-pasting the same SLA calculation logic into three separate flows instead of building one custom action?
options: Fixing a bug or rule change means finding and correctly re-editing all three, and missing one causes the flows to drift out of sync
There is no real cost — copy-pasting logic is just as reliable as centralizing it
The flows would stop triggering entirely
ServiceNow blocks duplicate logic across flows automatically
questions.explain: Centralized logic in a custom action gets fixed once and propagates automatically; duplicated logic has to be found and fixed everywhere it was copied.
